contexts.text: Every figment of the thoughts of his heart. SE 3353.

The figment of the thoughts of the heart () = no perception of good and truth... This deadly persuasion is here signified by the figment of the thoughts of the heart. But the figment of the heart, without the expression thoughts, = the evil of the love of self, or of cupidities. Illustrated.
That is a figment, which a man invents for himself, and of which he persuades himself. Illustrated.
The image-maker = him who persuades himself. Illustrated.
In general, a figment is that which a man invents from his heart or will, and from his thought or persuasion.
The figment of the heart of man is evil from his childhood () = that the Voluntary of man is altogether evil.
They thence invent a worship for themselves.
They thus invent doctrinal things for themselves.
Artificial and thus fictitious things of worship; that is, which are from proprium, or from the figment of the thought and of the heart of man. Signified.
That they invented a doctrine and a worship. Signified. AC 1313.
External confession... may exist in feigned humiliation, and in feigned affection of good...
Webs = fictitious or invented truths.
Hence a counterfeit, simulated, lying... principle reigns inwardly.
For man feigns what is honest; he feigns what is just...
A tool = truth invented; thus from proprium.
If a man has invented (what is false). Signified.
Fictitious zeal.
He is then like cunning feigners, who feign acts like human ones.
Spirits relate things very fictitious.
Influxes... fictitious, and thus simulated...
Representatives fictitious; and not fictitious. SE 4215.
A doctrine... from falsified truths and figments.
The adulteration of the Word by figments...
Confirming by fallacies, appearances, figments...
